investigations.name: composition-atlas
investigations.title: A composition atlas: building cell and tissue models by coupling simulators in every direction
investigations.description:
This investigation is a curated SHOWCASE of composition across modelling paradigms. The
unifying idea is the **semantics⊥mechanics split**: a model is written as semantics (a
reaction network, a Boolean logic, a scene of typed cells) and compiled onto mechanics
(an ODE integrator, a particle engine, a Boolean simulator, a tissue backend). Because the
split recurs at every scale, the same simulators compose in many creative directions.

**The CoupledCell foundation.** A new adapter,
`viva_multicell_blueprint.model_format.adapters.coupled.CoupledCell`, makes a cell whose
intracellular model is *itself a coupled composite* of several sub-models — each its own
formalism — wired by explicit coupling rules:
  * **mode A** — a source species crossing a threshold pins a target Boolean input;
  * **mode B** — a source species count sets a target ODE rate constant (live roadrunner);
  * **mode C** — a source Boolean node, when high, resets a target sub-model.
`CoupledCell` is itself an `IntracellularAdapter`, so it drops transparently into the
per-cell slot of the scene compiler — the tissue-scale composition, recursing one scale down.

**The atlas (studies).**
  1. `coupled-fate-oscillator` — ODE metabolism ↔ MaBoSS fate (modes A+C): C builds → pins
     the fate input → `divide` fires → division resets the metabolism → repeat. Two
     formalisms, one cell, a metabolism↔fate feedback oscillator.
  2. `coupled-particle-catalysis` — a Smoldyn particle population catalyses an ODE (mode B):
     the live particle C count sets the ODE's rate constant, so the ODE product accelerates
     as the particle population builds.
  3. `coupled-triple-cell` — all three formalisms AND all three modes in one cell: particles
     catalyse the metabolism, the metabolite pins the fate input, the fate output resets the
     metabolism. Particles → metabolism → fate → division, in a single cell.
  4. `fateful-tissue` — the full-stack crown: a dividing tyssue where each cell runs confined
     Smoldyn particles (split on division) AND an ODE→MaBoSS fate chain, and the fate output
     DRIVES the tissue division. Cells grow as they metabolise, divide when their own fate
     fires, and daughters reset and regrow — biology decides when the tissue divides.

**Companion axes (cross-links).** Two more composition axes are developed in sibling
investigations and complete the atlas:
  * sub-cellular ⟷ tissue (particles bounded by living cells, split on division) is the
    `particle-multicell-composition` investigation (the `bounded-particles-{cpm,vertex,munk}`
    studies) and the `scene-model-mixed-formalism` study;
  * tissue ⟷ tissue (CPM, vertex and center-based coupled into one consensus — vertex owns
    shape, munk owns position, CPM owns area) is the `tri_coupled` composite and its
    investigation.
investigations.question: This workspace has three tissue-scale simulators (Cellular Potts, vertex, center-based) and three sub-cellular simulators (SBML-ODE, Smoldyn particles, MaBoSS Boolean). How many genuinely different models can we build by COMPOSING them — coupling sub-cellular simulators to each other inside one cell, coupling sub-cellular to tissue, and coupling all scales at once — and what does each composition let us model that no single simulator can alone?
investigations.hypothesis: A model's SEMANTICS (what chemistry/logic it computes) are separable from its MECHANICS (which solver runs it), at every scale. If that is true, the same few simulators compose in many directions through small, explicit coupling contracts: a sub-cellular model is an adapter with a uniform interface, so several can run inside one cell coupled by typed rules (a product threshold pins a Boolean input; a particle count sets an ODE rate; a Boolean output gates a reaction); a cell is itself a coupled composite of such sub-models; and a tissue of these cells couples the sub-cellular scale back to mechanics — a cell's own metabolism→fate chain can even decide when the tissue divides. The atlas is the worked catalogue of those compositions, each a runnable composite with a visualization.

investigations.name: influenza-crossparadigm
investigations.title: Blueprint to pipeline to three substrates: one backend-neutral blueprint, run faithfully on CPM, vertex and center-based, with a pluggable subcellular layer
investigations.description:
This investigation covers the `viva-multicell-blueprint` pipeline end to end: the
backend-neutral blueprint (a versioned, statically validated artifact), the single
`blueprint_pipeline` composite that compiles it onto a mechanics backend, the three
real backends running the full model (reaction-diffusion fields, rules, a systemic
immune ODE fed live by cell counts, latent-pool immune recruitment, per-cell
subcellular ODEs), the comparison layer (`viva_multicell_blueprint.compare`: identity,
raster, metrics) and the interactive figures (`viva_multicell_blueprint.viz`).

**One composite.** `viva_multicell_blueprint.composites.pipeline.blueprint_pipeline`
(a `@composite_generator`, parameterized by `backend` and `blueprint`) is the baseline
composite for every study and drives the Composite Explorer. The earlier
`sego_crossparadigm` composite is a thin alias that delegates to it.

**Five studies.**
  1. blueprint-pipeline-fidelity -- the blueprint contract and t0 fidelity on every backend.
  2. cross-paradigm-equivalence -- fate and position equivalence across the three
     substrates, with the same-backend null and a mechanics-dominated positive control.
  3. substrate-behavior-at-scale -- distance-to-CPM behavior metrics on the large
     Sego tissue, and how the vertex mechanics were matched to the CPM.
  4. dose-response-crossparadigm -- all three substrates agree on the sign of the
     dose response.
  5. subcellular-layer-grow-divide -- the pluggable per-cell ODE layer grows and
     divides cells on all three backends.

**Three substrates, not two.** The center-based model (viva-munk: each cell a circular
rigid body, area-matched to the blueprint `size`) is compiled from the SAME canonical
blueprint via `local:MunkBackend`, shown as a third panel in every spatial playback,
and scored pairwise (cpm-vertex, cpm-munk, vertex-munk). It is deliberately NOT
calibrated to the other two (docs/mechanics.md), so it is a genuinely independent
representation.

**Blueprint contents.** The Sego blueprint pre-places 12 size-25 latent immune cells
(M/NK/CD8_latent) at the tissue margins via `extra_blocks`; recruitment activates that
latent pool in place, and the `infected_seed` is scoped to the main epithelial block so
the latent pool never changes the infected count. All cells are size 25 (size-9 cells
dissolve). Parameters stay faithful to Sego 2022 params.yaml @ b952eec2.

**Reduced scale.** Influenza studies run at a TRACTABLE reduced scale (a 50x50-site
patch, a 6x6 epithelial block) so the runs complete; the large Sego tissue (120x120,
~225-cell epithelium) is used for behavior-metric characterization. This is a
demonstration, not paper scale, and the comparison is reproducible (fixed seeds).

**Anti-goal respected.** No parameter is tuned to force the backends to agree. Honest
divergence is reported.
investigations.question: Can ONE versioned, backend-neutral blueprint be translated by a single pipeline (`blueprint_pipeline`) and run faithfully on three different mechanical substrates -- a Cellular Potts model (viva-cpm), a vertex model (vivarium-tyssue) and a center-based model (viva-munk) -- including a pluggable per-cell subcellular layer (a tellurium ODE that grows and divides cells); and where do the substrates agree vs diverge when the shared mechanism is driven live? The Sego 2022 influenza model (ViralInfectionVTM) is the worked example for the comparison; a v2 subcellular growth/division blueprint is the worked example for the subcellular layer.
investigations.hypothesis: Because the field / rule / systemic-ODE / subcellular mechanism is compiled identically onto all three backends and only the single mechanics node differs, cell-FATE dynamics should be nearly backend-independent while exact SPATIAL position should diverge: each substrate samples the shared field at its own cell centroid and measures cell-cell contact through its own geometry. Divergence is a finding about the substrate, not a bug. Confirmed three-way: fate agreement is statistically EQUIVALENT across all three paradigm pairs while exact-position agreement is not for any pair (the spatial gaps are +0.093 cpm-munk, +0.126 cpm-vertex, +0.252 vertex-munk). A mechanics- dominated positive control shows the test rejects when it should, and the subcellular layer grows and divides cells uniformly on every backend.
